name: To Record Only Water for Ten Days

podcast.body: Released in 2001, this solo record was still considered avant-garde but more coherent than his previous two solo albums, which were recorded while he was heavily addicted to heroin. The album incorporated plenty of electronic elements, inspired by a newfound appreciation for bands like Depeche Mode, The Cure, and New Order. "It was still pretty avant-garde, but at least it was a little more coherent, mainly because the previous two albums were recorded while he was whacked out on heroin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 2

podcast.body: This album marked a significant shift towards professionalism following Frusciante's rehabilitation. While perhaps not as intensely creative or musically intricate as some earlier works, it is noted for being much more polished and technically superior from a recording standpoint. It showcased Frusciante's expanded musical palette, incorporating synthesizers, New Wave elements, and even a touch of metal, reflecting his growth into a more complete and complex musician. "es el disco más pulido y más trabajo de frustriante. Refleja muy bien ese trabajo profesional."

srcs.episode: La historia de John Frusciante: Talento, creatividad y guitarras.
